per_question.q: What is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and how does it differ from fine-tuning?

composed.answer:
Based on the wiki, relevant material for "What is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and how does it differ from fine-tuning?":
- [[concepts/retrieval-augmented-generation]] — The dominant paradigm for grounding LLM outputs in external knowledge: retrieve relevant documents at query time, inject them as context, and generate answers — now evolving into modular, agentic context engines.
- [[concepts/rag-evaluation]] — The discipline of measuring RAG system quality across three tiers — retrieval metrics (Precision@k, MRR, nDCG), generation metrics (faithfulness, hallucination rate), and operational metrics (latency, safety) — using frameworks like RAGAS and benchmarks like RAGBench.
- [[sources/rag-evaluation-metrics-benchmarks]] — Comprehensive guide to RAG evaluation covering retrieval metrics (Precision@k, MRR, nDCG), generation metrics (faithfulness, hallucination rate), benchmarks (RAGBench, CRAG), and frameworks (Ragas, ARES, LangSmith).

composed.answer:
Based on the wiki, relevant material for "At what scale does Karpathy argue index-based retrieval can replace vector-database RAG for a personal knowledge base?":
